newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast power eases with weather, supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast power eases with weather, supply.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot electricity prices fell Monday with some milder temperatures along the West Coast and reports that the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) had put no limits on the size of power blocks it was offering, industry sources said.
"Even though the BPA average (price) was a little bit higher there was no limit on block sizes, which meant there was a lot of supply out there," said one Houston-based physicals trader.
BPA was reportedly offering power at an average of $19.20 for August 27, an increase from prices offered over the weekend.
Although temperatures in much of the West were expected to remain above normal, the heat was easing somewhat from last week, the sources said.
California-Oregon Border (COB) prices for firm, peak delivery were quoted at $19.00-20.00 from prices at $20.00-21.00 for Monday delivery, the sources said.
September COB power for firm, peak delivery was assessed at $18.00-18.50 from Friday discussion at $18.50-19.25 per megawatt hour (MWh).

Further north at the Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) delivery point in Washington, firm, peak electricity prices for next-day delivery were quoted at $16.00-18.00 from near $20.00 for Monday deliver, the brokers and marketers said.
September Mid-C electricity was pegged at $17.00-17.50 from a range of $17.75-18.40 per MWh, the sources said.
At the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard close to Phoenix, Ariz., next-day electricity for peak, firm delivery was valued at $23.00-24.00 from a range of $22.50-23.50 for Monday delivery, the sources said.
September firm, peak PV was quoted at $21.00-21.50 from a range of $21.00-22.00 in Friday discussion.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
